title: Classifying Living Things
seo_title: Primary 3 Science: Classifying Living Things Worksheets (with Answers)
standard_code: Primary 3: Diversity of living and non-living things (Classification of living things)
standard_text: Classify living things into broad groups: plants (flowering and non-flowering), animals, fungi and bacteria, based on their characteristics. Observe that fungi do not make their own food and that some bacteria are useful and some are harmful (summary of the MOE Primary Science Syllabus).
meta_desc: Free Primary 3 science worksheets for Singapore pupils on classifying living things: plants, animals, fungi and bacteria, mammals, birds, fish, amphibians, reptiles and insects. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Group living things by what they have in common.
key_sub: Plants, animals, fungi and bacteria; then mammals, birds, fish and more.
body_html:
How to think about it

Living things are grouped by their characteristics: plants, animals, fungi and bacteria.

  • Plants: flowering plants (make flowers and seeds) and non-flowering plants such as ferns and mosses (make spores).
  • Animals: mammals (fur, milk), birds (feathers), fish (scales, gills), amphibians (moist skin), reptiles (dry, scaly skin), insects (6 legs, 3 body parts).
  • Fungi: mushrooms, moulds and yeast. They cannot make food and reproduce by spores.
  • Bacteria: too small to see without a microscope. Some are useful, some are harmful.
Example

A bat can fly. Is it a bird?

Check the body covering: it has fur

It feeds its young with milk

Answer: No, it is a mammal.

Example

A mushroom grows on a dead log. Is it a plant?

It is not green

It feeds on the dead log and makes spores

Answer: No, it is a fungus.

Common mistakes

  • Classifying by where an animal lives or how it moves. A whale is not a fish and a bat is not a bird.
  • Thinking a spider is an insect. It has eight legs and two body parts.
  • Thinking mushrooms are plants. They are fungi and cannot make food.
  • Thinking all bacteria are harmful. Some help to make yoghurt and keep us healthy.

faq.a: No. A mushroom is a fungus. It is not green, cannot make its own food and reproduces by spores.

faq.q: Why is a whale a mammal and not a fish?
faq.a: A whale breathes with lungs, has a little hair and feeds its young with milk. Fish breathe through gills.
No. Some bacteria help us make yoghurt and live in our gut, while others cause diseases such as food poisoning.

items.q: Into which four groups can living things be classified?
items.e: Rocks and water are not living.

items.q: Which group of living things does a rain tree belong to?
items.e: Plants are green and make their own food.

items.q: Which characteristic do all mammals have?
items.e: Whales and humans also have some hair.

items.q: Why do we classify living things?
c: to group them by their characteristics so they are easier to study
to count how many there are
items.e: Living things with the same characteristics are put in the same group.

items.q: Which group of animals does a clownfish belong to?
items.e: A clownfish has scales and fins, so it belongs to the fish.

items.q: How many body parts does an insect have?
items.e: Head, thorax and abdomen.

items.q: Which group of living things does the mould on an orange belong to?
items.e: Fungi cannot make their own food. They feed on dead or decaying matter and reproduce by spores.

items.q: Which characteristic do all birds have?
items.e: Penguins and ostriches cannot fly, but all birds have feathers.

items.q: Which group of animals does a squirrel belong to?
items.e: A squirrel has hair or fur, so it belongs to the mammals.

items.q: Is a rain tree a flowering or a non-flowering plant?
items.e: It makes flowers, which become fruits with seeds.

items.q: How many legs does an insect have?
items.e: All insects have six legs.

items.q: Which group of animals does an eagle belong to?
items.e: An eagle has feathers, so it belongs to the birds.

items.q: Which group of animals does a chameleon belong to?
items.e: A chameleon has dry, scaly skin, so it belongs to the reptiles.

items.q: Which group of living things does a durian tree belong to?
items.e: Plants are green and make their own food.

items.q: Which group of living things does bread mould belong to?
items.e: Fungi cannot make their own food. They feed on dead or decaying matter and reproduce by spores.

items.q: Which group of plants makes flowers?
items.e: Ferns and mosses are non-flowering plants.

items.q: Is a water lily a flowering or a non-flowering plant?
items.e: It makes flowers, which become fruits with seeds.

items.q: How do fish breathe?
items.e: Gills take in air dissolved in water.

items.q: How does a bird's nest fern reproduce?
items.e: A bird's nest fern is a non-flowering plant. It reproduces by spores.

items.q: Which group of living things does the bacteria that cause tooth decay belong to?
items.e: Bacteria are living things too small to be seen without a microscope.

items.q: Which of these animals is a fish?
items.e: A seahorse has fins and gills.

items.q: A bat can fly. Why is it classified as a mammal?
c: It has fur and feeds its young with milk.
items.e: Flying does not make an animal a bird.

items.q: Which group of animals does a turtle belong to?
items.e: A turtle lives in water but has dry, scaly skin and lungs, so it is a reptile.

items.q: A whale lives in the sea. Why is it NOT a fish?
c: It breathes with lungs and feeds its young with milk.
It is too big to be a fish.
items.e: Whales are mammals.

items.q: Which of these animals is a bird?
items.e: A pigeon has feathers.

items.q: An animal has a pair of feelers (antennae) and three body parts. Which group does it most likely belong to?
items.e: An animal that has a pair of feelers (antennae) and three body parts belongs to the insects.

items.q: Which group of animals does a goat belong to?
items.e: A goat has hair or fur, so it belongs to the mammals.

items.q: Which of these animals can fly but is NOT a bird?
items.e: A butterfly is an insect.

items.q: Which group of animals does a butterfly belong to?
items.e: A butterfly has three body parts and six legs, so it belongs to the insects.

items.q: A spider has eight legs and two body parts. Is it an insect?
c: No. Insects have six legs and three body parts.
items.e: A spider is not an insect.

items.q: An animal breathes through gills all its life. Which group does it most likely belong to?
items.e: An animal that breathes through gills all its life belongs to the fish.

items.q: Which group of animals does a toad belong to?
items.e: A toad has moist skin without scales, so it belongs to the amphibians.

items.q: Which group of animals does a monitor lizard belong to?
items.e: A monitor lizard has dry, scaly skin, so it belongs to the reptiles.

items.q: Which of these animals is an amphibian?
items.e: A salamander has moist skin without scales.

items.q: A frog lays its eggs in water. Its tadpoles breathe through gills. Which group is it in?
items.e: Amphibians have moist skin and young that live in water.

items.q: Which of these animals is a reptile?
items.e: A crocodile has dry, scaly skin.

items.q: Which of these animals is an amphibian?
items.e: A toad has moist skin without scales.

items.q: A gecko has dry, scaly skin and lays eggs on land. Which group is it in?
items.e: Reptiles have dry, scaly skin.

items.q: Which of these animals is an insect?
items.e: A bee has three body parts and six legs.

items.q: Which of these is a mammal that lays eggs?
items.e: The platypus is a rare mammal that lays eggs, but it feeds its young with milk.

items.q: Why is a mushroom NOT a plant?
c: It is not green and cannot make its own food.
It grows in the dark, so it is non-living.
It has no leaves, so it is an animal.
items.e: A mushroom is a fungus.

items.q: Where do fungi get their food?
c: by making it in green leaves
items.e: Fungi feed on things such as dead leaves, bread or fruit.

items.q: Is a lalang grass a flowering or a non-flowering plant?
items.e: It makes flowers, which become fruits with seeds.

items.q: How does a horsetail reproduce?
items.e: Ferns, mosses, liverworts and horsetails make tiny spores.

items.q: How does a moss reproduce?
items.e: Ferns, mosses, liverworts and horsetails make tiny spores.

items.q: Which of these is made with the help of bacteria?
items.e: Bacteria turn milk into yoghurt.

items.q: Which group of living things does a moss belong to?
items.e: Plants are green and make their own food.

items.q: Which group of living things does a mushroom belong to?
items.e: Fungi cannot make their own food. They feed on dead or decaying matter and reproduce by spores.

items.q: How does a fern reproduce?
items.e: Ferns, mosses, liverworts and horsetails make tiny spores.

items.q: Which group of living things does a hibiscus plant belong to?
items.e: Plants are green and make their own food.

items.q: Why do we need a microscope to see bacteria?
c: Bacteria only come out at night.
Bacteria are too small to be seen with our eyes.
Bacteria are invisible in the day.
items.e: Most bacteria are made of just one tiny cell.

items.q: How do fungi such as mushrooms reproduce?
items.e: Fungi make tiny spores.

items.q: Which of these is made with the help of yeast?
items.e: Yeast, a fungus, makes bread dough rise.

items.q: How does a maidenhair fern reproduce?
items.e: A maidenhair fern is a non-flowering plant. It reproduces by spores.

items.q: Is a orchid a flowering or a non-flowering plant?
items.e: It makes flowers, which become fruits with seeds.

items.q: Which group of living things can make its own food?
items.e: Plants are green and make food using sunlight.

items.q: Which group of living things does an earthworm belong to?
items.e: Animals feed on other living things and most can move from place to place.

items.q: Is a durian tree a flowering or a non-flowering plant?
items.e: It makes flowers, which become fruits with seeds.

items.q: Which statement about bacteria is correct?
c: Some bacteria are useful and some are harmful.
items.e: Bacteria in yoghurt are useful; bacteria that cause food poisoning are harmful.

items.q: Which condition helps bread mould to grow fastest?
items.e: Fungi grow well in warm, moist places.

items.q: Which of these animals is a fish?
items.e: A tilapia has scales and fins.

items.q: Which animal does NOT belong to the same group as the others: hornbill, owl, toad, ostrich?
items.e: The others are birds. A toad belongs to the amphibians.

items.q: An animal has dry, scaly skin. Which group does it most likely belong to?
items.e: An animal that has dry, scaly skin belongs to the reptiles.

items.q: Which animal does NOT belong to the same group as the others: salamander, guppy, toad, frog?
items.e: The others are amphibians. A guppy belongs to the fish.

items.q: Which of these animals is a fish?
items.e: A stingray has scales and fins.

items.q: An animal lays eggs in water and its young breathe through gills. Which group does it most likely belong to?
items.e: An animal that lays eggs in water and its young breathe through gills belongs to the amphibians.

items.q: Which animal does NOT belong to the same group as the others: bee, moth, goldfish, ant?
items.e: The others are insects. A goldfish belongs to the fish.

items.q: Which of these is NOT an insect: ant, centipede, grasshopper, ladybird?
items.e: Insects have three body parts and six legs. The centipede has many legs.

items.q: Which animal does NOT belong to the same group as the others: cobra, python, crocodile, penguin?
items.e: The others are reptiles. A penguin belongs to the birds.

items.e: Insects have three body parts and six legs. The earthworm has no legs.

items.q: Which animal does NOT belong to the same group as the others: tilapia, mynah, clownfish, shark?
items.e: The others are fish. A mynah belongs to the birds.

items.q: An animal has feathers and wings, and lays hard-shelled eggs. Which group does it belong to?
items.e: This is a key characteristic of birds.

items.q: Which of these is NOT an insect: cockroach, dragonfly, ladybird, millipede?
items.e: Insects have three body parts and six legs. The millipede has many legs.

items.q: Ravi found a plant with no flowers. Under its leaves are rows of brown dots. What are the dots?
items.e: Ferns make spores in brown spore cases under their leaves.

items.q: Why are the slices of bread in a mould experiment kept the same size and type?
c: so that the bread stays dry
so that the test is fair
so that the mould grows slower
to make the bread taste better
items.e: Only one thing (the place) should be different.

items.q: Which animal does NOT belong to the same group as the others: kingfisher, guppy, eagle, chicken?
items.e: The others are birds. A guppy belongs to the fish.

items.q: Which group of animals does a mousedeer belong to?
items.e: A mousedeer has hair or fur, so it belongs to the mammals.

items.q: An animal starts life in water as a tadpole-like larva and later lives on land. Which group does it belong to?
items.e: This is a key characteristic of amphibians.

items.q: Ahmad left two slices of bread for a week: one in a warm, damp cupboard and one in a fridge. Which slice had more mould?
c: the slice in the warm, damp cupboard
items.e: Mould grows faster where it is warm and damp.

items.q: A pupil sorted animals into two groups: Group A (mynah, chicken, owl) and Group B (bat, cat, goat). What is the most likely way she sorted them?
c: lives in water / lives on land
items.e: Bats fly but are in Group B, so flying is not the rule.

items.q: An animal breathes with lungs and gives birth to live young that drink milk. Which group does it belong to?
items.e: This is a key characteristic of mammals.

items.q: A pupil sorted animals into Group A (frog, toad, salamander) and Group B (gecko, crocodile, cobra). What is the most likely way she sorted them?
c: lives in water / lives on land
items.e: Amphibians have moist skin; reptiles have dry, scaly skin.

items.q: Which group of animals does a frog belong to?
items.e: A frog has moist skin without scales, so it belongs to the amphibians.

items.q: Which characteristic would best tell a fish from a dolphin?
items.e: Fish breathe with gills; dolphins breathe air with lungs.

items.q: An animal has six legs, three body parts and a pair of wings. Which group is it in?
items.e: Insects have six legs and three body parts. Many also have wings.

items.q: Which group of animals does a pigeon belong to?
items.e: A pigeon has feathers, so it belongs to the birds.

items.q: Which animal does NOT belong to the same group as the others: frog, salamander, toad, pangolin?
items.e: The others are amphibians. A pangolin belongs to the mammals.

items.q: Which animal does NOT belong to the same group as the others: eagle, penguin, hornbill, cobra?
items.e: The others are birds. A cobra belongs to the reptiles.

items.q: Siti found a living thing in a damp forest. It is not green, has no leaves and grows on a dead log. Which group is it most likely in?
items.e: It feeds on the dead log, like a fungus.

items.q: Which animal does NOT belong to the same group as the others: ladybird, frog, salamander, toad?
items.e: The others are amphibians. A ladybird belongs to the insects.

items.q: Which group of animals does a catfish belong to?
items.e: A catfish has scales and fins, so it belongs to the fish.

items.q: Mei Ling put a drop of yoghurt under a microscope and saw tiny rod-shaped living things. What were they most likely?
items.e: Yoghurt is made with the help of bacteria.

items.q: Which animal does NOT belong to the same group as the others: mousedeer, hornbill, owl, eagle?
items.e: The others are birds. A mousedeer belongs to the mammals.
